subject: physics
question_text: State the laws of rolling friction.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty. AI physics check 2026-08-24: formulas, signs, numbers and claims verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; corrections applied to explanation text (why / common_mistakes / memory_tip), marked answer lines unchanged unless factually wrong.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: What it is
lines: When one body rolls over the surface of
another, the friction between them is
steps.margin_note: Define it before listing the laws. One line, then move on.
steps.why: Rolling friction is a different mechanism from sliding friction, so it gets its own laws and its own coefficient.
common_mistakes: Defining sliding friction by mistake and then listing the rolling laws under it.

recall.must_convey: That rolling friction is the friction when one body rolls over another.
accept: friction when a body rolls over another
oka body inkoka daani meeda roll ainapudu

steps.memory_tip: A rolling body never drags — a new point touches down each instant. That is the difference.

steps.label: The three laws
lines: 1. The smaller the area of contact, the
2. The larger the radius of the rolling
3. It is directly proportional to the
steps.margin_note: Three numbered laws. Each is one sentence — do not explain them, the question says "state".
steps.why: These are the board statements, and they are what earns the marks. The physical cause behind all three is the same: rolling friction comes from the surfaces deforming under the load, so anything that reduces the squashing reduces the friction. Read law 2 as a good approximation, not an exact law.
common_mistakes: Writing that rolling friction is independent of the area of contact. Area-independence is a law of SLIDING friction; rolling friction depends on the contact area (law 1) and is proportional to the normal reaction (law 3).

recall.must_convey: At least two of the three laws: smaller contact area, larger radius, proportional to normal reaction.
accept: smaller area of contact less friction
directly proportional to the normal reaction
reject: friction when a body rolls over another

steps.memory_tip: Three quantities in order: contact AREA, rolling RADIUS, normal REACTION. Smaller, larger, proportional.

steps.label: The coefficient
lines: Writing the third law as an equation,
where μ_R is the coefficient of rolling
steps.margin_note: Finish with the formula and name the symbol. A boxed equation with an unnamed symbol is half an answer.
steps.why: The coefficient is just the constant that turns the proportionality of law 3 into an equation you can put numbers into.
common_mistakes: Using μ without the R subscript, which is the sliding coefficient.

recall.must_convey: That F_R = μ_R N, where μ_R is the coefficient of rolling friction.
accept: F R equals mu R into N
reject: smaller area of contact less friction

steps.memory_tip: Steel wheel on rail gives μ_R near 0.001, against μ_k near 0.5 for sliding steel.

insider_note: Half the marks sit in the three numbered laws. Write the book’s three as printed — the examiner is ticking a list, not reading an argument.
